arxiv-2011-11831.title: Dissecting Image Crops
arxiv-2011-11831.creator: Basile Van Hoorick, Carl Vondrick
arxiv-2011-11831.description: Abstract The elementary operation of cropping underpins nearly every computer vision system, ranging from data augmentation and translation invariance to computational photography and representation learning. This paper investigates the subtle traces introduced by this operation. For example, despite refinements to camera optics, lenses will leave behind certain clues, notably chromatic aberration and vignetting.

arxiv-2012-12550.title: Invidious Comparisons: Ranking and Selection as Compound Decisions Thanks: Version: August 8, 2026. This paper was presented as the Walras-Bowley Lecture at the 2020 World Congress of the Econometric Society, and is dedicated to the memory of Larry Brown who introduced us to empirical Bayes methods.
arxiv-2012-12550.creator: Jiaying Gu, Roger Koenker
arxiv-2012-12550.description: Abstract . There is an innate human tendency, one might call it the “league table mentality,” to construct rankings. Schools, hospitals, sports teams, movies, and myriad other objects are ranked even though their inherent multi-dimensionality would suggest that – at best – only partial orderings were possible.

Cho, Aeree Chung, Eun Jung Chung, Hui-Hsuan Chung, Christopher J. R. Clark, David L. Clements, Timothy A. Davis, Ilse De Looze, David J. Eden, Gayathri Athikkat-. Observing nearby galaxies with submillimeter telescopes on the ground has two major challenges. First, the brightness is significantly reduced at long submillimeter wavelengths compared to the brightness at the peak of the dust emission.

arxiv-2202-07881.title: The addition of temporal neighborhood makes the logic of prefixes and sub-intervals EXPSPACE-complete \lsuper *
arxiv-2202-07881.creator: Laura Bozzelli ORCID:0000-0003-0963-8169, Angelo Montanari ORCID:0000-0002-4322- 769X, Adriano Peron ORCID:0000-0002-7111-3171, Pietro Sala ORCID:0000-0002-2612-1519
arxiv-2202-07881.description: Abstract . A classic result by Stockmeyer [ Sto74 ] gives a non-elementary lower bound to the emptiness problem for generalized ∗ * -free regular expressions. This result is intimately connected to the satisfiability problem for the interval temporal logic of the chop modality under the homogeneity assumption [ HMM83 ] .

arxiv-2204-09193.title: Functional Calibration under Non-Probability Survey Sampling Thanks: Zhonglei Wang and Xiaojun Mao contribute equally.
arxiv-2204-09193.creator: Zhonglei Wang
arxiv-2204-09193.description: Abstract Non-probability sampling is prevailing in survey sampling, but ignoring its selection bias leads to erroneous inferences. We offer a unified nonparametric calibration method to estimate the sampling weights for a non-probability sample by calibrating functions of auxiliary variables in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space.

arxiv-2303-10720.title: Trainable Projected Gradient Method for Robust Fine-tuning
arxiv-2303-10720.creator: Junjiao Tian Xiaoliang Dai Chih-Yao Ma, Zecheng He Yen-Cheng Liu Zsolt Kira
arxiv-2303-10720.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Junjiao Tian Xiaoliang Dai Chih-Yao Ma, Zecheng He Yen-Cheng Liu Zsolt Kira. Recent studies on transfer learning have shown that selectively fine-tuning a subset of layers or customizing different learning rates for each layer can greatly improve robustness to out-of-distribution (OOD) data and retain generalization capability in the pre-trained models. However, most of these methods employ manually crafted heuristics or expensive hyper-parameter searches, which prevent them from scaling up to large datasets and neural networks.

arxiv-2311-01198.title: Gaussian Processes on Cellular Complexes
arxiv-2311-01198.creator: Mathieu Alain, So Takao, Brooks Paige, Marc Peter Deisenroth
arxiv-2311-01198.description: Abstract In recent years, there has been considerable interest in developing machine learning models on graphs to account for topological inductive biases. In particular, recent attention has been given to Gaussian processes on such structures since they can additionally account for uncertainty. However, graphs are limited to modelling relations between two vertices.

arxiv-2503-06541.title: A stochastic force model for a finite-size spherical particle in turbulence
arxiv-2503-06541.creator: Yuqi Wang, Ruifeng Hu
arxiv-2503-06541.description: Abstract Predicting particle-laden flows requires accurate fluid force models. However, a reliable particle force model for finite-size particles in turbulent flows remains lacking. In the present work, a fluid force model for a finite-size spherical particle in turbulence is developed by simulating turbulent flow past a fixed spherical particle using particle-resolved direct numerical simulation (PRDNS).

arxiv-2503-14649.title: RAGO : Systematic Performance Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Serving Thanks: ∙ Work done while at Google ♦ Equal advising
arxiv-2503-14649.creator: Wenqi Jiang ∙, Suvinay Subramanian, Cat Graves, Gustavo Alonso, Amir Yazdanbakhsh ♦, Vidushi Dadu ♦
arxiv-2503-14649.description: Abstract . Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which combines large language models (LLMs) with retrievals from external knowledge databases, is emerging as a popular approach for reliable LLM serving. However, efficient RAG serving remains an open challenge due to the rapid emergence of many RAG variants and the substantial differences in workload characteristics across them.

arxiv-2505-09771.title: Grasp EveryThing (GET): 1-DoF, 3-Fingered Gripper with Tactile Sensing for Robust Grasping
arxiv-2505-09771.creator: Michael Burgess 1 and Edward H. Adelson 1
arxiv-2505-09771.description: Abstract We introduce the Grasp EveryThing (GET) gripper, a novel 1-DoF, 3-finger design for securely grasping objects of many shapes and sizes. Mounted on a standard parallel jaw actuator, the design features three narrow, tapered fingers arranged in a two-against-one configuration, where the two fingers converge into a V-shape.

arxiv-2507-22468.title: Conjugate phase retrieval on graphs and with applications in shift-invariant spaces Thanks: This project is partially supported by National Key RD Program of China (No. 2024YFA1013703), National Natural Science Foundation of China (12171490, 12371104), China Scholarship Council (202306380270, 202506
arxiv-2507-22468.creator: Cheng Cheng, Baixiang Wu, Jun Xian
arxiv-2507-22468.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cheng Cheng, Baixiang Wu, Jun Xian. In this paper, we study the conjugate phase retrieval for complex-valued signals residing on graphs, and explore its applications to shift-invariant spaces. Given a complex-valued graph signal 𝐟 \bf f residing on the graph 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , we introduce a graph 𝒢 𝐟 {\mathcal{G}}_{\bf f} and show that its connectivity is sufficient to determine 𝐟 \bf f up to a global unimodular constant and conjugation.

pmc-12454876.title: Improving emergency care capacity with the WHO-ICRC Basic Emergency Care (BEC) course
pmc-12454876.creator: Boris Arnaud Nteungue Kouomogne, Bissouma-Ledjou Tania, Chanceline Bilounga Ndongo, Alvine Choula Noulala, Hyppolite Kalambay Ntembwa, Pierre Claver Kariyo, Baonga Ba Pouth, Douba Epée, Bitang Louis Joss, Bertolt Brecht Kouam Nteungue, Dieudonnée Reine Ndougou, Mochache Trufosa, Simon Tumusiime, Amb
pmc-12454876.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundGlobally, the demand for acute care is surging, disproportionately burdening low- and middle-income countries. Training for healthcare providers can play a pivotal role in reducing related mortality and improving overall health and well-being, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite the potential for impact, the World Health Organization- International Committee of the Red Cross (WHO-ICRC) Basic Emergency Care (BEC) course is yet to be fully rolled out in Francophone African nations such as Cameroon, Djibouti, Haiti, Morocco, and Tunisia.

pmc-12503084.title: Does e‐cigarette nicotine strength influence substitution for combustible cigarettes?
pmc-12503084.creator: Jeffrey S Stein, Allison N Tegge, Jeremiah M Brown, Kelsey M Curran, Warren K Bickel
pmc-12503084.description: Using the Experimental Tobacco Marketplace, we examined the effects of e‐liquid freebase nicotine strength (3–24 mg/mL) and e‐liquid price (US$0.25–$1.00/mL) on behavioral economic substitution for cigarettes in dual cigarette/e‐cigarette (n = 41) and exclusive cigarette (n = 40) users. Subjective effects of nicotine strength were also examined.

pmc-12556176.title: The effect of ambient air pollutants on cardiac arrhythmia hospital admissions in Ireland
pmc-12556176.creator: K I Quintyne, C Kelly, P Kenny
pmc-12556176.description: AimExposure to poor ambient air quality and cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been investigated in numerous studies; whether ambient air pollutants are a cause of development of CVD, however, remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationship between COVID-19 transport restrictions and hospital admissions due to CVD specifically cardiac arrhythmias in Dublin city and county for 2020.

pmc-12691204.title: Structured Symptom Assessment in Dermato-Oncology Patients—A Prospective Observational Study of the Usability of a Symptom Questionnaire
pmc-12691204.creator: Martin Gschnell, Jannis Thole, Lisa Kroenig, Marianne Arz, Armin Bender, Michael Hertl, Christian Volberg
pmc-12691204.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummarySkin cancer patients often experience symptoms that can signal changes in their disease or side effects from treatment, but doctors currently lack a simple, reliable way to record these symptoms early and consistently. This study set out to test whether a standardised symptom checklist, completed by patients before seeing their doctor, could help identify troubling symptoms more effectively and guide treatment decisions.

pmc-13079740.title: A dataset on topsoil salinization characteristics in the Tailan River Irrigation District on the northern margin of the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang
pmc-13079740.creator: Qianxi Zhang, Miaomiao Gong, Wei Luo, Jingtong He, Jinhua Ding, Pingan Jiang
pmc-13079740.description: Soil salinization is a critical barrier to sustainable agriculture and ecological stability in arid and semi-arid regions. The Tailan River Irrigation District in southern Xinjiang is severely affected by salinization, with a two-decade absence of comprehensive soil salinity survey data hampering effective saline-alkali land management.

pmc-13204337.description: This study characterizes novel cross-linked polymeric composites based on bisphenol A glycerolate dimethacrylate (BPA.DM) as the primary matrix, incorporating 1-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone (NVP) or 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) as active diluents, and modified with antimicrobial agents: zinc oxide (ZnO), copper(II) sulfate (CuSO4), nanosilver (Ag), and benzethonium chloride (BEN).

pmc-13226377.title: A study of the interference colors of the microscopic textures simulated along the lyotropic phase sequence: cholesteric discotic–cholesteric biaxial–unwound cholesteric calamitic
pmc-13226377.creator: D. D. Lüders, E. Akpinar, G. E. Delmanoco
pmc-13226377.description: The interference colors of the microscopic textures, observed under a polarized microscope for the oriented cholesteric discotic (ChD)–cholesteric biaxial (ChB)–unwound cholesteric calamitic (NC*) phases sequence in the presence of a magnetic field, were studied in this work. The referred textures were interpreted from both experimental and theoretical views.

pmc-13279812.creator: Yannis Theocharis, Spyros Kosmidis, Jan Zilinsky, Friederike Quint

pmc-13287549.title: Haplotype‑resolved comparison of transcription factor superfamilies between wild and cultivated autotetraploid green jujube and prioritization of candidate transcription factors via machine learning
pmc-13287549.creator: Xudong Zhu, Pengyan Chang, Yanzhen Liao, Huini Wu, Fan Jiang
pmc-13287549.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A framework beyond single‐reference genomes is needed to understand transcription factor evolution. This study employed an integrated haplotype‑resolved genomes–transcriptome atlas–machine learning to characterize the transcription factors of autotetraploid green jujube (Ziziphus mauritiana). The first haplotype‑resolved comparison of transcription factor superfamilies from eight haplotype genomes (HapGenome) representing a specific wild and a specific cultivated green jujube accession, encompassing 42 superfamilies and 12,123 gene copies.

pmc-13300631.title: Efficiency and safety analysis of ultrasound-guided vs fluoroscopy-guided venous access for implantation of cardiac electronic devices
pmc-13300631.creator: D Parfianowicz, P Mahajan, R Sharma, M Shah, A Anandaram, P Neerumalla, R Ho
pmc-13300631.description: BackgroundUltrasound-guided venous access (UGVA) has been adopted by many procedural fields and has the advantage of forgoing radiation exposure to patients. To date, there are only small retrospective studies and a few randomized controlled trials that have evaluated short-term data regarding the safety and efficiency of ultrasound-guided placement of cardiac electronic devices (CED).

pmc-13339644.creator: Emma Audi, Carly M. Zack, Esther M. Ntankwa, William Blake Heston, Annika S. Waples, Manana Tsiskarishvili, C. Rose Kennedy, Shuming Chen, J. Patrick Lutz

pmc-13400829.creator: Zakari Adeiza David, Kareem Sarafadeen Olateju, Audu Godwin Amoka, Mustapha Omenesa Idris, Adefila Adebimpe Moyosore

pmc-13471674.title: Impact of climate on mental health among university students: a population-based study across 43 cities in China
pmc-13471674.creator: Tingzhong Yang, Ruoxiang Cao, Sihui Peng
pmc-13471674.description: Individuals are often exposed to multiple climate factors simultaneously, but there is limited research on the combined effects of these factors on mental health. This study aims to explore the simultaneous impact of temperature, humidity, and the number of sunny days on mental health, as well as the potential social and behavioral mechanisms underlying these associations.

pmc-13522552.title: Impacts of land use land cover change on ecosystem services of Hoto area, Gofa zone, South Ethiopia
pmc-13522552.creator: Medhanit Ketema, Shetie Gatew
pmc-13522552.description: Ecosystems provide critical services essential for human well-being and environmental sustainability. This study examines the impacts of land use land cover (LULC) dynamics on ecosystem service values (ESVs) in Hoto area, South Ethiopia, from 1993 to 2023. Using multispectral Landsat imagery, analyzed with ERDAS IMAGINE 2014 and ArcGIS 10.

pmc-13566567.title: αHSA-proIL-12: A Tumor-Conditional IL-12 Prodrug with Reduced Systemic Toxicity and Potent Antitumor Activity
pmc-13566567.creator: Xi Wang, Liu Yang, Yuhao Hou, Guanyu Wang, Yu Ding, Yu Zhang, Shuyu Wang, Zhangyong Hong
pmc-13566567.description: Interleukin-12 (IL-12) potently promotes the recruitment and activation of immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), highlighting its immense potential for cancer therapy. However, its dose-limiting systemic toxicity and short half-life severely hinder its clinical translation. Here, we design a tumor-conditionally activated IL-12 prodrug termed αHSA-proIL-12.

pmc-13613900.title: Beyond Analyte Recovery: A Holistic Review of Conventional and Miniaturized Extraction Techniques for Pharmaceutical Analysis in Environmental Samples
pmc-13613900.creator: Masimba Tapera, Tshimangadzo S. Munonde, Gcina Mamba, Ramakwala C. Chokwe, Lawrence M. Madikizela
pmc-13613900.description: The presence of pharmaceuticals in the environment has become a significant analytical and ecological concern because of their continuous release, persistence, and potential adverse effects. Their occurrence at trace levels, combined with the complexity of environmental matrixes, necessitates efficient extraction and preconcentration prior to instrumental determination.
